title: ChapterScenePlan
description: Artifact Contract (ADR-002) for a per-chapter SCENE PLAN: the paced beat skeleton the drafting prompt renders. v2 (Phase 4.2) DEMOTES the scene plan to a LOWERING of the Chapter IR (chapter-ir.schema.json): the production compiler now runs outline -> chapter-ir -> scene-plan -> prompt, and the scene plan is one scene per IR beat, in order, carrying the IR beat's narrative operations lowered onto the scene. A scene plan is a DERIVED artifact (ADR-006: it is design, not a fact); it is written to registry/derived/scene-plan/, never to registry/facts/, and carries provenance pinning the sources it was derived from so staleness is detectable (ADR-006). v2 is a BACKWARD-COMPATIBLE superset of v1: every v2 addition (per-scene turning_point/emotion_shift/information_gain/reader_question and top-level ir_ref) is OPTIONAL, so a v1 scene plan -- and a bare deterministic skeleton, and an LLM-enriched plan -- all still validate. Schema validity is DETERMINISTIC and may gate a single plan; the narrative quality of the beats is EVALUATIVE and never gates (ADR-003).

outline_ref.description: The outline artifact id this plan drew chapter intent from, or null when the chapter had no outline entry and the plan degraded to the chapter goal.

ir_ref.description: v2: the Chapter IR artifact id this scene plan was lowered from (chapter-ir.schema.json). Present when the plan was produced by lowering an IR (the v4 path); absent for a v1 plan folded directly from the outline. Links the scene plan to its IR for staleness/audit.

beat.description: The structural role of this scene in the chapter's beat skeleton.

purpose.description: What this scene must accomplish (one line).

participants.description: Characters on stage in this scene (fact ids).

conflict.description: The pressure/opposition active in this scene.

turn.description: The reversal or shift the scene delivers, if any.

exit_hook.description: The pull into the next scene/chapter, if this scene ends on one.

information_gain.description: v2 (lowered from the Chapter IR beat): what the reader newly LEARNS in this scene -- a reveal, clue, or raised stake. The anti-注水 signal: a scene that teaches nothing is a candidate to cut. Optional; a v1 plan omits it.

reader_question.description: v2 (lowered from the Chapter IR beat): the open question this scene plants or sharpens in the reader's mind -- the curiosity pulling them forward. Optional; a v1 plan omits it. NOTE: the IR's `turning_point` lowers to this scene's `turn`, and its `emotion_shift` lowers to this scene's `emotion`; only information_gain and reader_question had no v1 home.

pov.description: The point-of-view character this scene is narrated through (a fact id). Optional enrichment from the LLM scene planner; the deterministic skeleton omits it. Keeps viewpoint consistent within a scene.

emotion.description: The scene's emotional target. Optional enrichment; the sequence of `valence` across a chapter's scenes forms an emotion curve the drafting prompt follows for pacing.

tone.description: A short tone label (e.g. 压抑 / 紧张 / 爽快 / 温情).

beats_within.description: Optional micro-beats inside the scene (2-4), giving the drafter a shot list rather than a single line. Optional enrichment; the skeleton omits it.

text.description: What happens in this micro-beat (one line).

enrichment.description: Present only when an LLM scene planner enriched the deterministic skeleton (pov/emotion/beats_within). EVALUATIVE and never gates (ADR-003): `gating` is always false. `degraded` true means the enrichment failed and the scenes are the skeleton unchanged.

psych_beats.description: True when the enricher was given the character-runtime psych block and asked to land each lead's standing inner state as concrete in-scene actions inside beats_within (§12.1 ② follow-up). False/absent = the generic enrichment. Records which experimental arm produced this plan.
